title: I wrote the perfect manual for making a video game. I followed every step. Here's the result.
author: FJWY
selftext:
Solo dev here. I wrote the definitive guide to making a video game. Seven simple steps, zero errors guaranteed.

I followed all of them. The result has no START button, a sign that says THE BRIGDE, a Hero who is just a head, and "Made in Itlay" on the box.

Then I remembered that nobody reads the manual. So I made the manual the whole game.

The Game Manual is a comedy point-and-click for Android. Your only tool is the instruction booklet of a 1996 game that never came out. Whatever is written in it comes true, so when the world is broken, you change the manual.

15 chapters, 40+ puzzles, English and Italian. Free, with ads between chapters.

Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ilmanualedelgioco.il\_manuale](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ilmanualedelgioco.il_manuale)

P.S. The typos are intentional. Most of them.

comments.author: NSTStudios
comments.body: Was the beginning sequence what happens in the game? Maybe you can include more scenes of in game stuff And make it clearer how it works? Because for me the trailer seems like a bunch of preamble setting up the game but then not showing what actually happens in the game itself.

replies.author: FJWY
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! Actually, that's exactly what happens in the game! You're supposed to build the video game itself from scratch, following the instructions in the manual. The opening sequence shows this process, and the whole game revolves around it. You're not just preparing to play a game you're actually creating one inside the game!

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Hey u/FJWY, this falls under Rule 4. Commercial posts are okay here, but you need to talk about how it was developed using AI, so the community has something to discuss. This post doesn't have enough on that yet.

To keep it up, edit your post or reply to this comment within an hour with some details on your dev process, like:

- which AI tools you used, and what for
- how they fit into your workflow
- problems you hit and how you dealt with them

"Made with AI", a list of tools or a ChatGPT bullet list won't cut it. If nothing's added by then, this post may be removed.

If you think we got this wrong, [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev).
